Trump Reacts to the Election Results The Senate flipped. The House flipped. So how did President Donald Trump react? The Associated Press has called 33 of the 35 Senate races — Democrats and their independent allies hold 54 seats to Republicans' 44 — and the AP has called the House for the Democrats. Alaska and Mississippi are still counting, and no winner has been called in either race. Trump stayed publicly silent for about three hours on election night. Then he posted on Truth Social: “I wasn't on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP.” By phone, he told The New York Times he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results, and he told CBS News: “My message is, congratulations to the Democrats, and I look forward to working with you for the good of our country.” He also posted an image of his red cap stencilled with the word VETO, and called the veto “the ultimate power.” President Trump made no on-camera remarks about the results — his reactions were Truth Social posts and telephone interviews, so his words here are read aloud by our narrator from the cited reporting and shown as labeled text cards. No broadcast audio is used. Every reaction from both parties — Schumer, Thune, the winners, the concession — is in our full video: “Election Results: America Reacts.” Results and counts: Associated Press, Nov 4, 2026.
